case.case_title: Priyankara v. PC Sisira Kumara, Police Station, Puttalam and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, SC Application No 214/96 (Spl.), decided on 21 May 1998

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was unlawfully detained without being produced before a judge as required by Article 13(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed he was detained in custody for several days without being produced before a Magistrate or judge, violating Article 13(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents denied arrest and detention, claiming no justification for arrest and that the petitioner was not held or detained unlawfully.
key_facts: Petitioner was locked up in a police cell after assault at the police station.
Petitioner remained in custody from 15th to 17th October 1996 without being produced before a Magistrate.
Petitioner was hospitalized due to injuries sustained during detention.
Respondents denied arrest and detention, claiming no arrest was made.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(2) requires that any person detained must be brought before a judge and cannot be held without a legal order. The petitioner’s detention without production before a Magistrate violated this constitutional safeguard.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The petitioner was detained in a police cell for days without being produced before a judge, breaching Article 13(2). The respondents’ denial was rejected based on the petitioner’s credible evidence and circumstances.
principles_established: Detention without production before a judge is unlawful under Article 13(2).
Police must comply with legal procedures for detention to protect fundamental rights.

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner’s rights under Article 13(2) were infringed by the respondents due to unlawful detention without judicial oversight.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Compensation and costs as ordered for the infringement of fundamental rights.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) was central to the court’s finding that the petitioner was unlawfully detained without being brought before a judge, constituting a violation of fundamental rights.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner was kept in custody from 15th to 17th October 1996 without being produced before a Magistrate, violating Article 13(2).
